pages.step_question_ko: 🧭 [연결 질문] 보조선이 만들어 낸 공통변이나 엇각·동위각 중 서로 크기가 같은 것은 어디일까요?

pages.visual_focus: 증명 도형 단계별 작도 (단계별 수학적 추론 및 증명 전개)
pages.explanation_text: 2단계, 2페이지 단계입니다. 주어진 점들과 직선을 포함하는 기준 평면을 설정하고, 교선과 수선의 발을 내려 공간 관계를 평면 위의 합동·평행 관계로 환원하는 보조선을 중심으로 도형에서 서로 길이가 같은 변과 크기가 같은 각을 하나씩 짝지어 비교합니다.

narrations.en: Step 2 (Page 2). Set a reference plane containing given points and straight lines, and compare sides of the same length and angles of the same size in the figure one by one, centered on auxiliary lines that reduce spatial relationships to congruent and parallel relationships on the plane by lowering the intersection and perpendicular lines.

pages.step_question_ko: ⚠️ [오개념 점검 질문] 증명할 결론을 미리 가정으로 끌어다 쓰는 순환논리 실수를 피하려면 무엇을 확인해야 할까요?
pages.step_question_en: ⚠️ [Misconception check question] What should I check to avoid the mistake of circular logic, which is drawing conclusions in advance into assumptions?
pages.visual_focus: 증명 도형 단계별 작도 (단계별 수학적 추론 및 증명 전개)
pages.explanation_text: 3단계, 3페이지 단계입니다. 한 직선 위에 있지 않은 서로 다른 세 점은 단 하나의 평면을 결정한다는 기본 공리로부터 두 직선의 교점·평행선 및 수직 관계를 단계별로 연역하는 원리가 완성되는 단계입니다. 이때 꼭 기억해야 할 점은, 평면기하에서는 만나지 않는 두 직선이 무조건 평행하지만, 3차원 공간에서는 만나지도 않고 평행하지도 않은 '꼬인 위치'가 존재하므로 반드시 한 평면 위에 있는지 먼저 확인해야 합니다!

narrations.en: Step 3 (Page 3). This is the stage where the principle of deducing step by step the intersection, parallel line, and perpendicular relationship of two straight lines is completed from the basic axiom that three different points that are not on a straight line determine only one plane. What you must remember at this time is that in planar geometry, two straight lines that do not meet are unconditionally parallel, but in three-dimensional space, there are 'skew lines' that neither intersect nor are parallel, so you must first check whether they are on the same plane!

According to the spatial geometry axioms and plane determination conditions that we tried to prove from the correspondence between shapes, 'all points on a straight line passing through two different points on a plane are on this plane.' We can confirm that the geometric conclusion that the property is unique and necessarily holds is necessarily true.

narrations.en: Step 5 (Final Step): The visual proof is complete! Starting from the starting condition of 'All points on a straight line passing through two different points on a plane are on this plane' given the basic axioms and positional relationships of points, straight lines, and planes in three-dimensional space, which were the starting conditions, we set a reference plane containing the given points and straight lines, go through the auxiliary lines that lower the intersection and perpendicular lines to reduce spatial relationships to congruent and parallel relationships on the plane, and then 'two different points on one plane' according to the axioms of space geometry and plane determination conditions. 'All points on a straight line passing through it lie on this plane.' We have clearly confirmed that the geometric conclusion that properties are unique and necessarily true holds true. The key point to remember here is that in planar geometry, two straight lines that do not meet are unconditionally parallel, but in three-dimensional space, there are 'skew lines' that neither intersect nor are parallel, so you must first check whether they are on the same plane! Finally, ask a deeper question. If we expand the perpendicular conditions of straight lines and planes in this space, how will it be connected to the formulas of 'Theorem of Three Perpendiculars' and 'Area of the Orthogonal Projection (S' = S cos θ)', which are the core of high school geometry?
